en: The Banaue Rice Terraces act as giant inclined planes, reducing the force needed for farmers to carry heavy harvests up the mountain.
Jeepney drivers apply brakes to increase friction between the rubber tires and the road, stopping the vehicle safely on wet streets.
Gravity pulls falling coconuts straight down toward the ground, which is why farmers in Quezon province wear hard hats during harvest.
The black sand beaches of Ilocos contain magnetite, a naturally magnetic mineral that can attract small iron filings.
The MakBan geothermal power plant in Laguna converts heat energy from underground volcanoes into the electricity that powers nearby homes.
Fireflies in the mangroves of Bohol produce bioluminescence, a chemical reaction emitting cold light to attract mates without generating heat.
Sound travels faster through the solid bamboo poles of a traditional bahay kubo than through the surrounding air.
Farmers in Zambales use solar dryers to absorb heat from the sun, quickly drying mangoes to prevent spoilage.
The swinging bamboo poles in the Tinikling dance possess kinetic energy, while the elevated poles have potential energy.
The sharp blade of a traditional bolo acts as a wedge, converting downward swinging force into a splitting force.
Rubbing a dried calamansi leaf against a plastic comb transfers electrons, creating static electricity that attracts small paper pieces.
Earth's gravity exerts a stronger downward pull on a heavy sack of Nueva Ecija rice than on a single grain.
